schemes.evidence: DESIGNATION 1. Paragraph 4 of the official Ealing Cabinet designation PDF applies the scheme to the three council ward areas of East Acton, Southall Broadway and Southall Green, expressly marked (pre May 2022 ward boundaries), as edged red on the Annex A map. Corroborated by Ealing's own page https://www.ealing.gov.uk/info/201086/housing/3306/private_rented_properties/8, which states the council adopted the scheme from 1 April 2022 for those wards on pre-May-2022 boundaries. All three ward names survived the 2022 review but their boundaries changed, so they are not current-ward equivalents. No street list or postcode list was published for Designation 1, and Ealing operates no address or postcode checker. Ealing has NOT restated either selective designation against post-2022 wards. Both sealed designations and the council's live map still name pre-May-2022 wards, while The London Borough of Ealing (Electoral Changes) Order 2020 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/65/made) abolished the existing wards with effect from the May 2022 elections. currentWards is deliberately left empty: the LGBCE final recommendations show the review re-cut boundaries rather than simply renaming wards (for example Perivale lost Perivale Lane and Leaver Gardens to Pitshanger, and minor modifications were made to Hanger Hill, North Greenford and South Acton), so even the surviving ward names no longer describe the designated area.

inForce.howVerified: Start read from the body of Ealing's own page https://www.ealing.gov.uk/info/201086/housing/3306/private_rented_properties/8 ('and from 3 January 2023'). Duration from the Cabinet minute of 15 June 2022, which designates the area for a five-year period; five years from 3 January 2023 ends 2 January 2028. No sealed notice stating the cessation date verbatim was found on any official site, so the end date is calculated from those two official statements; the scheme is in force today 7 August 2026 either way.

wardMapping.note: Abolished. The LGBCE final recommendations state it was not possible to retain the existing Acton Central ward and that ward boundaries were redrawn across the whole of Acton, so its area was redistributed among the redrawn Acton wards (Ealing Common, East Acton, North Acton, South Acton, Southfield). Neither the order nor the report states a one-to-one successor, so none is asserted.

Derived and approximate. LGBCE paragraphs 55 to 57 discuss the existing Greenford Green ward alongside the new Central Greenford ward and reject a request to name the new ward Greenford Green, indicating Central Greenford is the successor. Boundaries are NOT identical: paragraph 56 records a southern extension of the Central Greenford boundary across the A40.

Derived and partial. LGBCE paragraph 89 records that respondents proposed Hobbayne South as an alternative name for the new Hanwell Broadway ward, indicating Hanwell Broadway covers part of the former Hobbayne ward. The remainder is not identified in the report, so this mapping is incomplete.

schemes.evidence: DESIGNATION 2. Paragraph 4 of the Cabinet designation PDF (https://ealing.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s1214/Appendix%201%20Selective%20Licensing%20Designation%202.pdf) and the Cabinet minute of 15 June 2022 (https://ealing.moderngov.co.uk/mgAi.aspx?ID=486) both apply the scheme to the twelve council ward areas of Acton Central, Dormers Wells, Greenford Broadway, Greenford Green, Hanger Hill, Hobbayne, Lady Margaret, North Greenford, Northolt Mandeville, Northolt West End, Perivale and South Acton, expressly marked (pre May 2022 ward boundaries). The streets array is transcribed from the council's own Appendix 2 street list (https://ealing.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s1215/Appendix%202%20Selective%20Licensing%20Designation%202%20Streets.pdf), titled 'List streets by ward area (pre-May 2022 boundaries)', covering all twelve wards; it is the most precise official definition of the area and sidesteps the stale-ward problem entirely. It was reconstructed from a wrapped three-column PDF, so a small number of long footpath and access-way descriptions may be imperfectly joined; all ordinary named streets were verified clean and alphabetically consistent. No postcode list exists and Ealing publishes no checker; its only public aid is a ward map (https://www.ealing.gov.uk/download/downloads/id/19918/map.jpg) which also still uses pre-2022 ward names. Ealing has NOT restated either selective designation against post-2022 wards. Both sealed designations and the council's live map still name pre-May-2022 wards, while The London Borough of Ealing (Electoral Changes) Order 2020 (https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/65/made) abolished the existing wards with effect from the May 2022 elections. currentWards is deliberately left empty: the LGBCE final recommendations show the review re-cut boundaries rather than simply renaming wards (for example Perivale lost Perivale Lane and Leaver Gardens to Pitshanger, and minor modifications were made to Hanger Hill, North Greenford and South Acton), so even the surviving ward names no longer describe the designated area.
